Why do cats purr?

Cats purr for several reasons. Most commonly, purring indicates contentment and happiness. However, cats also purr when they're in pain, anxious, or giving birth. Scientists believe the vibrations from purring may promote bone healing and growth. When your cat is sitting on your lap purring, they're typically showing affection and trust.

How long do cats live?

The average lifespan of a domestic cat is between 12 to 18 years, though some cats live into their 20s. Indoor cats typically live longer than outdoor cats due to reduced exposure to dangers like traffic and predators. Factors that influence longevity include genetics, diet, exercise, veterinary care, and lifestyle. Some of the longest-lived cat breeds can reach 20+ years with proper care.

Do cats really have nine lives?

The myth about cats having nine lives likely originated in ancient Egypt, where cats were highly revered. In reality, cats have just one life, but they do have remarkable agility, flexibility, and instincts that help them survive falls and dangerous situations better than many other animals. Their ability to land on their feet and their quick reflexes contribute to their reputation for being nearly indestructible, but they are not immortal.

Why do cats sleep so much?

Cats sleep an average of 12 to 16 hours per day, which is normal feline behavior. This is because cats are crepuscular animals, meaning they are most active during dawn and dusk. In the wild, this sleeping pattern conserves energy for hunting. Domestic cats maintain this instinct even though they don't need to hunt. All that sleep also helps their bodies rest and their brains process information.

Why do cats have whiskers?

Whiskers are highly sensitive tactile hairs called vibrissae that help cats navigate their environment. They can detect minute changes in air currents and help cats determine if spaces are wide enough for their body to fit through. Whiskers also serve as proximity sensors that protect the eyes and face from obstacles. Never trim a cat's whiskers, as they are essential for their spatial awareness and balance.

Can cats see in the dark?

While cats cannot see in complete darkness, they have superior night vision compared to humans. Their eyes contain more rod cells and a reflective layer called the tapetum lucidum that bounces light back through the retina, giving them the ability to see in very low light conditions. Cats need only one-sixth of the light that humans require to see clearly. However, they are not completely adapted to darkness and still need some ambient light.

How do cats communicate with each other?

Cats communicate through a combination of vocalizations, body language, and scent marking. Their meows are primarily directed at humans, while cats use a variety of other sounds like chirps, hisses, and yowls to communicate with each other. Body language, including tail position, ear orientation, and posture, conveys emotions and intentions. Cats also mark territory by rubbing their scent glands on objects and other cats, creating a chemical communication network.

Why do cats scratch furniture?

Scratching is a natural and essential cat behavior that serves multiple purposes. Cats scratch to sharpen their claws, stretch their muscles, mark territory by leaving scent and visual marks, and relieve stress. Scratching also helps cats shed the outer sheath of their claws. To redirect this behavior, provide appropriate scratching posts or pads in areas where your cat naturally wants to scratch, and use deterrents on furniture you want to protect.

Are all cats colorblind?

Cats are not completely colorblind, but they see color differently than humans. They see blues and greens well, but reds and pinks appear more greenish or brownish to them. The world appears somewhat desaturated compared to human vision, with blue and green hues being most vibrant. Despite having fewer color receptors than humans, cats' color vision is adequate for their hunting and daily needs. Their superior night vision and motion detection compensate for their limited color perception.

How can I keep my cat healthy?

Keep your cat healthy by providing a balanced diet appropriate for their age and health status, ensuring regular veterinary check-ups, maintaining a healthy weight, providing fresh water, and offering mental stimulation through play and enrichment activities. Regular grooming, including brushing teeth and trimming nails, is important for overall health. Ensure your cat is up-to-date on vaccinations and preventive medications. The average lifespan of a domestic cat is between 12 to 18 years, though some cats live into their 20s. Cats sleep an average of 12 to 16 hours per day, which is normal feline behavior. This is because cats are crepuscular animals, meaning they are most active during dawn and dusk.
